solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Churches grasping a new opportunity

indicators.note: grasping means the church letters hold the next pieces between them

parts.note: CH and CE are two abbreviations for church (CE = Church of England), so the plural gives both

explanation.surface: Congregations seizing a fresh opening for growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churches' supplies two separate church abbreviations, CH and CE, which 'grasping' splits around A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is an opening or favourable occasion to do something, the same as an opportunity.

clue.text: Keen to take over outlet in place of exile

indicators.note: to take means the word for keen holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a vent is an outlet for air or gas

explanation.surface: Someone eager to seize a shop in the land they were banished to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb to wail. 'Sent to Coventry' is a British idiom for being ostracised; Coventry is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone to Coventry is to shun them, so the city is figuratively a place of banishment.

clue.text: Curiously agree with lots of trusted friends

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, lots of trusted pals see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is a very close and trusted friend.

clue.text: Josh is under Charlie's bed

indicators.note: is under places the second piece below the first in this down entry

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to josh is to tease, to rib

explanation.surface: Josh is hiding under Charlie's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' and 'Charlie' look like two boys' names; both are pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a baby's cot, a small bed with barred sides.

clue.text: Start to shroud face with cape, revealing conceit

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: mug is slang for face
a ness is a headland or cape, common in place names

explanation.surface: Someone covering their face with a cloak and somehow giving away their vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive pride in oneself, which is exactly smug self-satisfaction.

clue.text: Cut back in funds? Nothing replaces European domination

indicators.note: replaces means one letter is swapped for another
in places the reversed cut inside the word for funds

parts.note: money means funds

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Budget cuts strike the funds as Brussels is pushed out by nothing in a power grab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOP to POL, set 'in' MONEY; then O 'replaces' the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopoly is exclusive control of a market, i.e. total domination of it.

clue.text: Piece of office equipment popular after many become involved in craft

indicators.note: become involved in means the pieces are taken into the word for craft

parts.note: guile means craft or cunning

indicators.note: after places the popular word behind the many word

parts.note: a lot means many
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A popular gadget once lots of people are drawn into crafting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like handicraft; it is cunning, GUILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillotine is also a paper cutter with a long blade, a staple of offices.

clue.text: Live departures with a twist in the tail

indicators.text: with a twist in the tail
indicators.note: a twist in the tail means the last letters of the word are turned round

parts.note: exits are departures

explanation.surface: Live departures boards with a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a twist in the tail' swaps the last two letters of EXITS. 'Live' looks like broadcast live but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive or to live.

clue.text: Upcoming races taking in northern beach

indicators.note: taking in means the reversed word encloses the next letter
upcoming in a down entry means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: darts means dashes or races

explanation.surface: Forthcoming races including one on a northern beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' turns DARTS to STRAD, 'taking in' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is a literary word for shore or beach.

clue.text: Many ships are fast

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means quick or fast

explanation.surface: A navy's ships are quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet names a group of vessels and, as an adjective, swift.

clue.text: Musical group overwhelmed by endless nasty, harsh criticism

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the band is swallowed up inside the other piece
endless means the word for nasty loses its final letter

parts.note: vile means nasty
a trio is a musical group of three

explanation.surface: A band drowned out by a nasty crowd's relentless abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical group' could be many bands; the four-letter trio fits the gap left after 'endless' trims the nasty word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol, literally sulphuric acid, is used figuratively for caustic, bitter criticism.

clue.text: Editing loses volume, then turns louder

indicators.note: turns means the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
loses means a letter is dropped from the word for editing

parts.note: revision is the act of editing a text

explanation.surface: A sound edit removes some volume, yet the track ends up louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes V out of REVISION, leaving REISION, which 'turns' then sends backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier is the comparative of noisy, making more sound, so it means louder.

clue.text: Standard portion of protein or meat

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A standard-sized serving of protein or meat on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or expected level, a standard against which things are measured.

clue.text: Italian citizen staggering into a plane

indicators.note: staggering suggests something reeling unsteadily, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian lurching drunkenly onto an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native or inhabitant of Naples, a city in Italy.

clue.text: Knit pants I wear, even tighter at the front

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered
at the front means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Knitting trousers to wear even tighter at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers; it is the anagram signal. The T from 'tighter' joins the letters of I WEAR EVEN in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit threads is to interlace them, the same as to interweave.

clue.text: Ruling on information technology, primarily

parts.note: re means on or concerning
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A legal ruling about information technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like a noun, a judgment, but it is the adjective, as in the Prince Regent.
explanation.definitionFit: Regent placed after a title describes one who rules on behalf of a monarch, so it means governing.

clue.text: On the whole, boring thing rang out loud

indicators.note: out loud says the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes, and tolled means rang like a bell

explanation.surface: Summing up an evening when a dull object kept ringing noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning in total or taking everything into account.

clue.text: See fine boxer, with first of knockouts, start to earn double

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
OK means fine
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word is used
start to means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A good boxer racks up knockouts and begins to earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a person who closely resembles another, i.e. their double.

clue.text: Calling on one to protest in very good surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the very good letters sit around the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sit-in is a form of protest

explanation.surface: Someone singled out to protest amid pleasant surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Visiting someone means calling on them, paying a call.

clue.text: Ring wife about large rears becoming muscular

indicators.note: rears means rises up, so in a down entry the letters read upward
about means the ring and wife letters go around the large letter

parts.note: to tinkle is to ring, as a small bell does

explanation.surface: A wife phones about her big behind that is toning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rears' looks like backsides; it is the verb rise up, reversing the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-knit describes a firmly built, sturdy body, so strong and muscular.

clue.text: Introduce American narcotic with nothing taken out

indicators.note: taken out means a letter is removed from the drug word, here the zero letter

parts.note: heroin is a narcotic drug
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drug case: American heroin with nothing missing from the haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher in is to mark the start of something or bring it in, i.e. introduce it.

clue.text: Proceeds company invested in abandoned mine

indicators.note: invested in means the company letters are placed within the others
abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm sinks money into a derelict mine to get a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as derelict in the surface but signals the shuffle of mine, around which the company abbreviation is set by 'invested in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are money received from a sale or activity, which is income.

clue.text: Special crest associated with southern states

parts.note: a peak is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: A special emblem tied to the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like the US southern states; it is the verb, says.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who states something speaks it, declares it.

clue.text: Spirit that's surrendered on dying?

definitions.meaning: to give up the ... is to die, so the ... is what is surrendered

explanation.surface: The soul that is yielded up at death.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost means spirit, and the idiom give up the ghost means to die.

clue.text: Coward, perhaps, unusually wary in sticky situation

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for a predicament

parts.note: a plight is a difficult or sticky situation

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of wary appear in a different order

explanation.surface: A coward, oddly cautious, stuck in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward was an English dramatist, so 'Coward' is a name, not a timid person; 'unusually' shuffles wary, and 'in' sets it inside the predicament word.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote plays such as Private Lives, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Heavenly messenger turning up in musical, eg "Nativity!"

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An angel appears in a school Nativity musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'in' signals it. In a down entry 'turning up' means read upward, so the hidden run is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a messenger of God, as in Gabriel at the Nativity.

clue.text: Nick's positive response in Germany and Israel

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is nick, slang for prison

parts.note: ja is German for yes
IL is the international code for Israel

explanation.surface: A man called Nick says yes in Germany and in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the nick is a prison or police station, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Reportedly overcrowded settlement

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: packed means overcrowded

explanation.surface: A settlement said to be bursting with people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a village; it is an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is an agreement settling terms between parties.

clue.text: A series of four letters entertains an Asian

indicators.note: entertains means the series holds a guest inside it

parts.note: FGHI is a run of four consecutive letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A sequence of letters hosting an Asian visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Any run of four consecutive alphabet letters could be meant; only the one that, wrapped round 'an' as 'entertains' says, makes a nationality works.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghani is a person from Afghanistan, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Boy captures French director in channel

indicators.note: captures means the boy word holds the director inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
Jacques Tati was a French film director

explanation.surface: A boy snares a French film-maker inside a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV or radio station is a broadcasting channel.

clue.text: Exercises for singer if legs go wobbly

indicators.note: wobbly suggests something unsteady, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's vocal drills that leave the knees shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Solfeggi (plural of solfeggio) are vocal exercises sung to the syllables do, re, mi.

clue.text: Box, for example, in extremely soft way

indicators.note: in places the tree inside the outer letters
extremely means only the letters at the extremes of the word are taken

parts.note: box is a kind of evergreen tree

explanation.surface: Boxing done in an unusually gentle manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like the sport; it is the shrub. 'extremely' gives ST from soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, and way is a common word for a road in names.
